observations: Adjacent, and in main's script too: e2e-local.sh exits 0 when interrupted. SIGINT or SIGTERM sent while it waits for listener health ends the run with status 0 after printing only 'waiting for listener health', because cleanup() reads rc=$? inside the trap, where it is 0. main's c9578e115b5a has the same 'cleanup() { local rc=$?' and 'trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM'. An interrupted acceptance that a caller sees as a pass is this tree's subject again. One fix: separate traps that pass 130 and 143 into cleanup. Sent to the architect, not failed here.

The new lock needs util-linux flock, which stock macOS lacks. The script now exits 3 there with 'required command is unavailable: flock'. Nothing in the repository says e2e-local.sh runs on macOS; CI is Ubuntu, and this pod has /usr/bin/flock.

If e2e-local.sh itself is killed with SIGKILL, its natsd and listener inherit the lock descriptor and outlive it, so the next run is refused with 'another run ... is using' until they are killed. They also hold the NATS port, so that run could not have passed anyway; the message is accurate in effect.
